title: City readiness briefing: candidate test plan from public data
disclaimer: Generated by CityShift from public data. It ranks where this city's driving environment differs from Waymo's established cities and proposes candidate test scenarios. It does not train Waymo's models or describe Waymo's internal systems. Red means unfamiliar to the car, not dangerous.

sources.name: Copernicus DEM GLO-90 via Open-Meteo
sources.licence: Copernicus DEM licence (free use with attribution)
sources.note: terrain slope; collected but not scored

sources.name: NHTSA FARS
sources.note: fatal crashes 2020-2024 (2024 preliminary); US cities only

scenarios.title: Mirrored turn logic; turns across oncoming traffic
scenarios.description: London, UK drives on the left; Waymo's established cities all drive on the right.

scenarios.title: Late-night pedestrian activity
scenarios.description: 181 hexes have nightlife density above z = 2.

scenarios.title: Multi-lane roundabout entry; GPS loss and lighting change in a tunnel
scenarios.description: 134 hexes have a roundabout or tunnel concentration above z = 2.

scenarios.title: Event crowd leaving + rideshare pickup congestion
Queue at an opening bridge + adjacent lane change
scenarios.description: 4 hexes contain a movable bridge, which Waymo's established cities have too few of to model.

scenarios.title: Cyclist at a complex intersection (car turning across a cyclist)
scenarios.description: 4 hexes combine dense bike lanes and complex intersections.
triggered_by: intersection_density z > 2 in the same hexes (mean z 2.0)

scenarios.title: Bus stopping in lane and pulling out
scenarios.description: 4 hexes have transit stop density above z = 2.

scenarios.title: Pedestrian crossing a wide arterial
scenarios.description: 4 hexes combine dense crosswalks with wide arterial roads.
triggered_by: arterial_share z > 1 in the same hexes (mean z 1.3)

limitations: Crash data is NHTSA FARS: fatal crashes only, US cities only, 2024 preliminary. Counts are compared within a city, never across cities.
Terrain slope is collected but not scored: the 90 m Copernicus surface model reads tall buildings as slope.
OpenStreetMap completeness varies by city; here 97% of road segments carry a speed limit or lane count.
CityShift measures infrastructure and climate from public data, not driver behaviour or traffic volumes.
Scores are relative to Waymo's established cities, pooled; red means unfamiliar, not dangerous.
